text:
Harper: Quick heads-up  I'm opening a single PR to tidy up Optimize toolkit docs: fix broken redirects after the examples reshuffle, replace legacy SDK snippets (streaming + prefetch) with v2 idioms, and add a small docs-linter workflow to catch these on future changes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4999 :package:
Diego: Sounds good. Which legacy snippets specifically?
Harper: A few places still use `client.stream()` and the old `prefetch()` call without context. Example files: examples/old/streaming_py.md, examples/cache/prefetch_example.md, and /optimize/quant/legacy_profiles.md references `q_profile_alpha`.
Zoe: Can you paste the new streaming snippet you'll use? Want to make sure it matches our canonical examples.
Harper: New Python streaming snippet we standardize on:

```python
# SDK v2 streaming (async iterable)
async for chunk in client.responses.stream(model="rwr/small"):
    if chunk.delta:
        print(chunk.delta, end="")
```

New non-streaming alternative for quick copy-paste:

```python
resp = client.generate(model="rwr/small", input="Summarize product goals")
print(resp.output_text)
```
Diego: Nice. For prefetch, prefer explicit context + TTL note?
Harper: Yep. Example added:

```python
with timeout(5):
  client.prefetch(model="rwr/small", max_tokens=1024)
# note: KV cache TTL defaults to 6h; set prefetch.TTL to change
```
Zoe: Great. About the docs-linter workflow  will it only run on files changed in the PR?
Harper: Yes, it's a lightweight GH Action that greps for legacy patterns (`client.stream\(|prefetch(`, `q_profile_alpha`) and fails only if `--strict` flag is enabled. By default it warns and posts a comment with matches.
DocsBot: Automated note: PR 4999 created by Harper. Reviewers: Diego, Zoe. Docs CI: link-checker + snippet-lint queued.
Diego: I'll review wording and ensure redirects are correct. If tests look good, we can merge midweek.
Zoe: I'll run the new snippets against staging SDK and report any API differences. Thanks for consolidating this into one PR  makes backfills much easier. :thumbsup:
